newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: U.S. to seek Chile trade pact before NAFTA entry.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to seek Chile trade pact before NAFTA entry.

text.p: The United States wants to sign a bilateral trade pact with Chile as a first step for that country to enter the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), a senior U.S. official said on Wednesday.
The United States, a partner of Canada and Mexico in NAFTA, earlier hoped to include Chile directly in the broader pact.

"Now it looks as if will be a bilateral kind of free trade agreement between the United States and Chile, which by necessity will look very similar to our NAFTA agreement," Richard Brown, U.S. senior coordinator for the Summit of the Americas, told Reuters.

Brown, participating in an international seminar on business transparency in Buenos Aires, said talks with Santiago could be delayed until after the next Summmit of the Americas scheduled for April in Chile.

Although it was expected that negotiations with Chile would start before April, negotiators from both sides are busy organising the summit and with preliminary negotiations over the Americas Free Trade Area (AFTA), he said.
"There's always the question of human resources. So it will probably have to be put off until after the Chilean summit."

Washington is leaning more toward a bilateral agreement than Chile's full entry into NAFTA in part because Santiago has already negotiated separate free trade pacts with Mexico and Canada, Brown said.
Once Washington's pact with Santiago is reached, officials will try to harmonise the other bilateral accords until Chile gets full access to NAFTA, he said.
"The other two partners will probably have to upgrade their bilateral agreements with Chile, I would think."
Brown reaffirmed that at the beginning of September the U.S. government will seek to overcome congressional opposition and negotiate with Chile with speedier fast-track authority.
The pact could be clinched before the year-end congressional holidays, he said.
President Bill Clinton will visit Chile for the second Summit of the Americas, which is expected to formally launch negotiations to form AFTA by 2005.
Clinton also plans to visit Argentina, Brazil and Venezuela.
